scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A refund on screen
scenes.caption: Asha expects a fictional festival refund of eight hundred rupees. A message asks her to scan a code and approve the next screen. In this simulation the screen is only a teaching artifact; no real code or payment exists.
scenes.dialogue: Read the authorisation, not only the message.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The direction is wrong
scenes.caption: The mock screen says pay eight hundred rupees from Asha to Refund Desk. That is outgoing authorisation, even though the message calls it a refund. The payee and amount need checking alongside the direction.
scenes.dialogue: An incoming promise can hide an outgoing instruction.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Payment evidence
scenes.caption: Receiving money does not require sharing an OTP or entering a UPI PIN to approve someone else’s payment. Use your own trusted bank or payment app to check a credit. A screenshot supplied by the sender is not your account record.
scenes.dialogue: Check who pays whom before confirming.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the safe action
scenes.caption: The screen authorises a debit to an unverified payee. Should Asha approve it to receive money, share her PIN with support, or cancel and verify the refund separately?
scenes.dialogue: The screen’s direction controls this decision.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Approval is cancelled
scenes.caption: Asha cancels the outgoing authorisation and checks through the school’s known festival contact. She keeps the message as evidence. A matching amount did not make the mismatched payee or outgoing direction safe.
scenes.dialogue: Eight hundred in the message was not eight hundred received.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the payment lab
scenes.caption: Inspect direction, payee and amount, distinguish a credit from a debit and respond when the beneficiary changes. Every amount and reference is fictional. There is no payment button connected to a bank.
scenes.dialogue: Practise the check before any real confirmation.
